neighbours.label: marking a cause as one of several joint contributors to an outcome (also/both contributed, combined with, another factor, compounding)
fire: Low interest rates and a shortage of new homes have both contributed to the rise in house prices.
Cheap flights, combined with a weak currency, drew record numbers of tourists last summer.
A second factor driving the decline in bee numbers is the loss of wild flowers.
The crash was caused by fog, and the driver's speed only added to the danger.
Bad weather also contributed to the delays, on top of the strike by port workers.
Compounding the problem, the city's only bridge was closed for repairs that week.
Long shifts coupled with poor sleep left many nurses exhausted by spring.
The drought hurt the crops, and the locust swarm made the situation even worse.
quiet: The mayor contributed a short essay to the town's anniversary booklet this year.
Cheap flights and a new hotel were both listed in the brochure we picked up last summer.
A second chapter of the report covers the history of bee keeping in the valley.
The crash happened on a foggy morning near the old railway station.
Several neighbours contributed cakes to the school fair on Saturday.
The city's only bridge is painted green and was built in 1910.
Long shifts and night work are part of a nurse's job in most hospitals.
The drought lasted three months and ended with a heavy storm in May.
